text: Gustave Flaubert's Madame Bovary led to a trial in France in 1857. Flaubert, the owner and the printer of La Revue de Paris were tried before the Tribunal correctionnel de la Seine over the serialised publication of the novel, accused of insulting public morals and offending decent manners. The trial ended on 7 February 1857, and the three men were acquitted in February 1857.
